messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] Hosted runtime: sudden KV cache OOMs observed across multiple shards in prod-west-2. Alert group: kvcache-ooms. Triggered 5m ago.
ops-oncall: seeing a big uptick in 5xxs and oom count on nodes serving long prompts. error rate ~3.8% -> 12% in last 10m. GPU mem flatline then OOM.
mira: which models/tenants are noisy? any particular session id patterns?
alec: mostly long-prompt sessions (chat threads > 120k tokens). Prefetch + continuous batching appears to amplify the window. Logs show prefetch queued huge kv entries.
samir: repro snippet from logs: 
```
kv_cache: insert(key=session:abc123, size=183MB)
kv_cache: current_size=12.8GB, max=13GB
runtime: OOM on alloc 256MB
```
liz: customer impact: a few high-throughput customers seeing 500s + slow tail latencies. CS has 2 tickets open, SLO blips on 3 routes.
kevin: can we temporary throttle prefetch or reduce per-session kv cap? we have feature flags but need a safe rollout.
ops-oncall: proposing immediate mitigation: disable continuous-prefetch for hosted runtime globally, and reduce batch_window_ms from 40ms -> 10ms for critical shard pool. That should cut prefix inflation.
mira: +1. Steps?
ops-oncall: 1) run config hotpatch to turn off prefetch on hosted. 2) push batch window change to runtime group id prod-west-2. 3) add eviction spike to clear oversized sessions older than 2h.
alec: commands I used in dev: 
```
# hotpatch prefetch
redwoodctl runtime set-config --cluster prod-west-2 --key runtime.kv.prefetch.enabled --value false --no-restart
# reduce batch window
redwoodctl runtime set-config --cluster prod-west-2 --key runtime.batching.batch_window_ms --value 10
# force eviction for sessions >2h
redwoodctl kvcache evict --cluster prod-west-2 --age 7200
```
support-eng: notifying affected customers with templated status message now. linking tickets: #CS-4931, #CS-4940.
deploy-bot: Rollout started: config hotpatch user=alec change=runtime.kv.prefetch.enabled:false target=prod-west-2 -- 1/3 shards patched.
ops-oncall: patching shards sequentially to avoid mass evictions; will monitor.
kevin: monitoring dashboards: OOMs per-node chart + kv_inserts_per_min. Pre-hotpatch inserts spike was 8x normal.
samir: quick check: any deployments or model rollouts in last 30m?
alec: none. Only pattern is large user prompts (customer scripts that concatenate transcripts).
liz: CS update: one high-value customer (org: XenoCorp) reported degraded responses; they are on dedicated SLA. flagged for escalation.
ops-oncall: temporarily raise capacity for XenoCorp pool and pin to a lighter model variant while we stabilize.
mira: do we have a safe fallback model with lower KV pressure? smaller seq-length config?
kevin: yes, model-lite-v1 uses shorter context stitching and limited prefetch; CPU cheap. Plan: route XenoCorp to model-lite-v1 via traffic policy.
samir: proposed SLA note: "We observed transient OOMs due to runaway KV cache growth triggered by long prompts + continuous prefetch. Temporary mitigations applied: prefetch disabled, batch window reduced, evictions forced; routing fallback for affected customers. Working on permanent limiter."
ops-oncall: live numbers after step1 (prefetch off on 2/3 shards): OOMs down 75%, 500s reduced to 1.5%. memory pressure dropping.
deploy-bot: Rollout complete: prefetch disabled on all shards. Change id: hotpatch-368500A.
alec: follow-up: we should push a throttling knob scoped per-tenant: max_kv_entries_per_session and hard cap on session bytes. Also add detection to block prefetch when session grows > X tokens.
mira: agreed. I'll open an RFC. For immediate safety, we should add an automatic circuit breaker: if kv_cache_total_growth_rate > 2GB/min for a shard -> throttle prefetch and start sample evictions.
support-eng: (typo) sorry, accidental.
kevin: customer routing for XenoCorp done. they confirm improved latency.
liz: CS updated customers for incident and ETA for permanent fix: 72 hours.
ops-oncall: action items:
- mira: RFC + breaker prototype (ETA 24h)
- alec: add per-tenant kv caps + admin override (ETA 48h)
- samir: dashboards + alerts tuned to growth rate (ETA 4h)
- kevin: postmortem draft and customer impact table (ETA 12h)
- ops-oncall: follow-up verify no regression during next 4h.
all: any objections to closing the pager after 1hr of stable metrics? :thumbsup: to close, :thumbsdown: to keep paging.
support-eng: :thumbsup:
kevin: :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: :thumbsup: closing at T+65m unless we see more OOMs.
mira: quick note for postmortem: correlate with continuous-batching config and longprompt sessions; include replay tests.
alec: saved command snippets and logs in incident runbook gist: https://gists.company/incident-3685009876
ops-oncall: closing thread, moving to incident tracking ticket INC-368500. Thanks everyone.
